Meet the consultants

01 Pain Management

Dr. Pallavi Dasyam

Consultant — Pain Management

MBBS, DA, CIPS — Certified Interventional Pain Sonologist, World Institute of Pain, USA.

Like most interventional pain physicians, Dr. Pallavi came to pain medicine through anaesthesia — the same drugs and the same needles, aimed at one structure instead of a whole body. The CIPS certification she holds from the World Institute of Pain is the international qualification for exactly that work: putting a needle where the ultrasound image says it needs to go, and not a few millimetres away.

She runs the consultation and the diagnostic scan herself, in the same room. Where the scan confirms what the examination suggested, the procedure follows in that appointment under local anaesthetic — you stay awake, and you can tell her what you are feeling while she works.

02 Pain Management

Dr. PSS Kiran

Consultant — Pain Management

MBBS, MD (Radiology), Fellowship in Pain Management — musculoskeletal intervention, sports and regenerative medicine.

Dr. Kiran read the scans before he began performing the procedures they point to. That radiology background is the reason a consultation here includes a diagnostic ultrasound rather than a referral for one: the person interpreting the image is the person who will treat what it shows, so nothing is lost between the report and the needle.

His fellowship is in pain management, with a working interest in musculoskeletal intervention, sports injury and regenerative treatment — the tendon, ligament and overuse problems where the aim is to get a structure healing again rather than simply to numb it.

Whichever of them you see, the appointment runs the same way.

01

One pair of hands

The consultant who examines you performs the scan, and performs the procedure if one is indicated. Nothing is handed to a second team, and nothing has to be explained twice.

02

The scan decides

Nothing is injected on a hunch. If the ultrasound rules out the structure the examination suspected, you leave with a different plan — not with a procedure you did not need.

03

Awake, and home the same day

Procedures are done under local anaesthetic as day care. No admission and no general anaesthetic, so most people are home within about two hours of arriving.

Procedures they perform

  • Radiofrequency ablation
  • COOLIEF cooled RF
  • Nerve blocks
  • Nerve hydrodissection
  • Prolotherapy
  • Regenerative medicine
  • Epidural & transforaminal injections

Ask for either of them by name.

Appointments are spaced through the day, so the wait is short. Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or scan reports you already have.
